_persona: GOLDEN — wages + long-term capital gain, 2026 epoch year. Expected values were hand-computed from cited primary sources BEFORE the model was run against them; they are not model output. See docs/GOLDEN_CASES.md.
_do_not_repin: These are external anchors, not self-consistency pins. If one of them moves, the model disagrees with the cited source — investigate the model, do not re-pin. scripts/repin_personas.py must always report 0 moved here.

_sources.rp_25_32: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 — 2026 single ordinary brackets, standard deduction $16,100, and LTCG rate ceilings: 0% top $49,450, 15% top $545,500. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf
_sources.irc_1411: IRC §1411 — Net Investment Income Tax: 3.8% x min(net investment income, MAGI − $200,000) for a single filer. Statutory, unindexed.
_sources.irc_3101b2: IRC §3101(b)(2) — Additional Medicare Tax 0.9% on wages over $200,000 (single). Statutory, unindexed.
_sources.ssa_2025_10_24: SSA announcement 2025-10-24 — 2026 Social Security wage base $184,500; max employee SS tax $11,439 (6.2%).

_excluded: CA bracket-derived fields (ca_taxable, ca_income_tax, total_tax, take_home, effective_tax_rate) carry no golden claim — the 2026 CA tables are still projected from 2025 actuals.

niit_agi_binding._source: wages 180,000 + LTCG 30,000. MAGI 210,000 sits just over the §1411 threshold, so the MAGI excess binds, not the gain.

2026._fed_taxable: ordinary taxable = AGI 210,000 − standard deduction 16,100 [rp_25_32] − LTCG 30,000 = 163,900 (the gain is removed and taxed on its own schedule)
2026._federal_ltcg_tax: ordinary taxable 163,900 already exceeds the 0% ceiling 49,450 [rp_25_32], so no part of the gain is free; the stack 163,900+30,000=193,900 stays under the 15% ceiling 545,500 => 30,000 x 15% = 4,500.00
2026._fica_social_security: min(180,000, 184,500) x 6.2% = 11,160.00 [ssa_2025_10_24] — under the wage base, so uncapped
2026._fica_additional_medicare: max(0, 180,000 - 200,000) x 0.9% = 0.00 [irc_3101b2] — the surtax is on wages, not on MAGI, so the 210,000 MAGI does not trigger it

niit_income_binding._source: wages 400,000 + LTCG 100,000. MAGI 500,000 is far over the §1411 threshold, so the investment income binds.

2026._fed_taxable: ordinary taxable = AGI 500,000 − standard deduction 16,100 [rp_25_32] − LTCG 100,000 = 383,900
2026._federal_ltcg_tax: stack 383,900+100,000=483,900 sits entirely between the 0% ceiling 49,450 and the 15% ceiling 545,500 [rp_25_32] => 100,000 x 15% = 15,000.00
2026._niit: 3.8% x min(inv income 100,000, MAGI 500,000 − 200,000 = 300,000) = 3.8% x 100,000 = 3,800.00 [irc_1411] — the investment income binds

niit_below_threshold._source: wages 150,000 + LTCG 20,000. MAGI 170,000 is under the unindexed $200,000 §1411 threshold.

2026._niit: MAGI 170,000 <= 200,000 threshold => 0.00 [irc_1411], regardless of the 20,000 gain
2026._fed_taxable: ordinary taxable = AGI 170,000 − standard deduction 16,100 [rp_25_32] − LTCG 20,000 = 133,900
2026._federal_ltcg_tax: ordinary taxable 133,900 exceeds the 0% ceiling 49,450; stack 153,900 stays under 545,500 [rp_25_32] => 20,000 x 15% = 3,000.00

ltcg_zero_bracket._source: wages 40,000 + LTCG 40,000. Ordinary taxable income is low enough that the gain straddles the published $49,450 top of the 0% LTCG bracket.

2026._fed_taxable: ordinary taxable = AGI 80,000 − standard deduction 16,100 [rp_25_32] − LTCG 40,000 = 23,900
2026._federal_ltcg_tax: the gain stacks on ordinary taxable 23,900: room under the 0% ceiling is 49,450-23,900=25,550 taxed at 0%; the remaining 40,000-25,550=14,450 falls under the 15% ceiling 545,500 => 14,450 x 15% = 2,167.50 [rp_25_32]
